newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan May trade surplus seen slipping.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan May trade surplus seen slipping.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Wednesday projected a US$1.1325 billion trade surplus in Taiwan for May, down 36.5 percent from a US$1.784 billion surplus in May 1996.
They projected a 7.78 percent year-on-year rise for export growth in May and a 17.96 percent annual rise in imports.
Official figures were to be issued by the Finance Ministry at 0245 on June 7.

The following table lists institutions' forecasts for May in billions of U.S. dollars and year-on-year percentage change. Brackets ( ) indicate negative growth. A dash -- indicates no comparison because of deficit against surplus or vice versa.
Institution Exports chg Imports chg Balance chg
April showed a trade deficit of US$204 million, with exports at US$9.839 billion and imports at US$10.043 billion.
In May 1996, exports were US$9.552 billion and imports were US$7.768 billion, giving a trade surplus of US$1.784 billion.
Economists noted that import growth has been persistently higher than export growth because of rising domestic demand in a modestly recovering Taiwan economy.
"Import growth should be larger than export growth, and a dwindling trade surplus is the trend -- at least for this year," said National Securities economist Lin Kuo-yang.
Economists said import growth also would be fuelled by a surge in imports of advanced weapons for Taiwan's rivalry with communist China, which spurred import growth in March and April.

Another factor would be strong consumer goods imports in May, spurred by spending of profits earned in Taiwan's big stock market rally, which had added 25 percent to the main stock index by the time it began a correction in late April.
Economists said they expected the Taiwan dollar's recent depreciation against the U.S. dollar to help exports.

"The depreciation should help increase Taiwan's exports, which will also be boosted by rebounding prices for integrated circuits and the introduction of new types of notebook computers," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
The Taiwan dollar had depreciated to T$27.88 to the U.S. dollar in late May from T$27.34 in mid-January.
-- Taipei Newsroom (8862-5080815)
